hook: You don't have a procrastination problem. You have a decision architecture problem.
topic: Environmental design — removing the decision points avoidance exploits
body:
**You don't have a procrastination problem. You have a decision architecture problem.**

Every time you sit down to work, your environment presents you with a set of choices. Phone visible or not. Notifications on or off. Browser open or closed. Inbox loaded or not. Each one of those is a decision point — and decision points are where avoidance lives.

The research on willpower is clear: it's a finite resource. Each decision depletes it. If your work environment is full of competing options, you will eventually choose the wrong one — not because you're weak, but because the cumulative weight of those micro-decisions erodes the capacity to resist them.

The solution is not stronger willpower. It's fewer decision points. Design your environment so that the right action is the easiest one available, and every competing option has been removed before the session starts.

The reframe: every structural change to your environment is worth more than any amount of motivational effort. One change to the room beats a hundred intentions inside your head.

One action: before tomorrow's first work session, do one environmental intervention — phone in a different room, one tab open, notifications off. One change. Start there.

Full environmental design framework in the link in bio.
